## Done since the last report

- **Incremental transcript feed.**
  - `status` no longer carries the transcript. A new `feed` message sends it, either all at once or as a small update that drops the oldest entries and adds the new ones.
  - The host sends everything again after a reconnect or when the selected session changes.
  - The firmware, the simulator and the fake device all handle it. Both sides have tests, and `proto/PROTOCOL.md` documents it.
- **"When Claude finishes" options merged.** The two settings are now one, `ask_when_finished`: a number of seconds away from the PC, `0` for always, `-1` for never. The tray menu, hook logic and tests are updated.
- **Decorative spinner verbs removed.** The screen now says "Working…" instead of a random verb. I regenerated the screenshot and fixed the layout SVG.

## Not done, on purpose

- **Web pairing page.** Replacing the native pairing dialogs with a local web page would mean adding an HTTP server and a new screen flow, which cuts against the simplification. The dialogs work, so I left them.
- **Folding the CI `publish` job.** It would save about 15 lines and add a race between the two release jobs, so I left CI alone.

I've implemented most of the plan and haven't committed anything. The host tests pass (98 passed, 1 skipped) and `ruff` is clean. The firmware simulator passes 21 tests, and the native text tests pass. I couldn't run the PlatformIO firmware build or flash a real keypad.

## What changed

- **Deleted features:**
  - the MCP `ask_user` tool and its heavy dependencies
  - the mic button
  - Arabic/RTL text
  - key-test mode, the debug firmware, and the light theme
  - the "tell Claude a keypad is connected" option
  - session persistence
  - per-keypad project filters
  - the update-check popup
  - the `service`, `claude` and `config` command-line verbs
  - the separate `keypad-hook` binary
  - PyYAML (config is now `config.json`)
  - `hw_regress.py`, the simulator's live viewer and walkthrough, and four doc files
- **Protocol v3:**
  - Wi-Fi is the only runtime link; USB handles pairing only.
  - The handshake is one hello each way, with no acks, resends or device-side announcements.
  - Battery and Wi-Fi state ride on `hello` and `pong`.
  - Message types dropped from about 22 to 18, listed in `proto/PROTOCOL.md`.
- **Live feed:** the agent now follows each session's transcript file, so Claude's text appears as it is written. Hooks shrank from 10 to 6 and only decide (permission, question, stop, prompt, session start/end).
- **Readable Markdown:** a real Markdown parser (`markdown-it-py`) lays out headings, lists, quotes, tables, code, links, bold and italics for the small screen. Unreadable characters are mapped to look-alikes. 14 golden tests cover it, and the firmware gained a dim style for italics. The regenerated `docs/img/screens.png` shows the result.
- **PC or keypad, first answer wins:**
  - The tray gets an "Answer requests on" setting: Both, Keypad only, or PC only.
  - If Claude moves on in the transcript while a request is open, or you type at the PC, the request is withdrawn and the hook returns no decision.
- **Client and build:**
  - The tray now runs the agent in the same process, with one login item instead of two.
  - Local IPC is loopback TCP with a token file, which removes the Windows named-pipe code, and its tests now run on Windows.
  - The PyInstaller spec lost its second binary.
  - The README now covers security, testing and releasing in one place.

An end-to-end smoke test (real agent, fake keypad, real hook call over the new IPC) returned "allow" correctly. The diff is roughly 2,800 lines removed and 1,000 added, plus about 600 lines of new modules and tests.

## What I did not do

- **Phase 0 spike not run.** I didn't check whether Claude Code shows its own terminal dialog while a permission hook is still blocking. That decides how "answer in the terminal" behaves. Typing at the PC and the transcript-based withdrawal are implemented either way. The README wording is hedged to match.
- **Protocol:**
  - The separate `feed` message for incremental transcript updates is not done; `status` still carries the transcript.
  - I kept the answer replay (`cachedPress`) on the keypad so a lost answer still survives a reconnect.
- **Pairing page and dialogs:** I did not replace the native pairing and settings dialogs with a local web page. That was too risky to do blind.
- **Smaller leftovers:**
  - I didn't merge the three "when Claude finishes" options.
  - I left the decorative spinner verbs and animated star in the firmware.
  - CI is unchanged.

## Before you rely on it

- **Firmware update:** an existing keypad needs one USB flash, since v2 and v3 can't talk to each other.
- **Settings reset:** old `config.yaml` settings are not carried over; the agent logs a note and starts from defaults.
- **Test on a keypad:** a real permission dialog and a real session feed.
